Demand shocks

Placeholder paragraph for the test fixture. A shift of aggregate demand moves the price level and real output in the same direction: more spending at every price level raises both, which is demand-pull inflation, and less spending lowers both. A shift of short-run aggregate supply moves them in opposite directions: higher input costs raise the price level and lower output, which is cost-push inflation, and in a severe case stagflation. Unemployment moves opposite to output in the short run, so a demand shock or a supply shock shows up in the labor market too. Each change is shown on the AD-AS graph with the price level on the vertical axis and real GDP on the horizontal axis.
